source.title: Limitations of the NTK for Understanding Generalization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Nikhil Vyas; Yamini Bansal; Preetum Nakkiran

record.tranche_reason: The study measures data-scaling on image-classification tasks with convolutional networks and corresponding NTKs, rather than language-model pretraining.
record.gate_note: The study reports fitted scaling exponents for test classification error as training-set size changes. This is not held-out language-model cross-entropy, and it does not sweep parameter count, tokens, or compute to test a compute-optimal allocation. Cited results from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study assumes a saturating power-law form, L(n)=A(1/n+α)^β, for binary image-classification test error. It uses the fitted exponent β only as a tool to compare finite CNNs with their empirical and infinite NTKs. It reports no goodness of fit and does not test whether the power law holds. It measures no language-model loss and does not sweep parameters, tokens or compute. Its findings are about the NTK, not about whether scaling laws hold.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that finite-width networks have better data-scaling exponents than their infinite and empirical NTKs at initialization. Kernels extracted after fixed training (after-kernels, or kernels at fixed time) also scale worse, and the empirical NTK keeps improving through most of training. Hence the NTK misses data-scaling behaviour. They also report that test error is non-monotonic in width, with very wide networks deteriorating toward the infinite NTK.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses image-classification test error and varies training-set size, comparing finite-width convolutional networks with empirical and infinite NTKs. It does not use language models, held-out cross-entropy, or parameter/token/compute scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported scaling constants vary with learning rate, optimizer choice, use of momentum, and early-stopping choice. The paper also compares widths and reports scaling differences between finite networks, initialization NTKs, and after-kernels. Scaling fits use L(n) = A(1/n + α)^β and least squares in log space.

fits_no_version.finding: Finite CNNs have larger data-scaling exponents for image test error than their empirical and infinite NTKs (.307 vs .185 and .213 on CIFAR-5m-bin; .28 vs .19 and .22 on SVHN-parity). The gap shrinks at a 1000x smaller learning rate (.204).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-scaling exponents of trained networks exceed those of their linearized/NTK counterparts at practical widths and learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: The image-classification data-scaling exponent of the same CNN shifts with training hyperparameters: .262–.333 across learning-rate, optimizer and early-stopping choices, and .204 at a very low learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitted data-scaling exponents in image classification depend on optimization hyperparameters.

fits_no_version.finding: At a fixed training size, test error of the CNN first improves and then worsens as width grows very large, approaching the infinite NTK (Fig 2b,c; Fig 8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test error is non-monotonic in width for NTK-parameterized networks.

record.problems: The evidence concerns binary image-classification test error rather than language-model cross-entropy. The infinite NTK is represented by a single run; the text notes that some empirical-NTK high-width results were not rerun, and that some experiments were limited by computational feasibility. Several plotted results are described qualitatively rather than with tabulated values.
record.rows_left_out: Qualitative width-sweep outcomes, after-kernel performance versus training-set size, and empirical-NTK time-dynamics findings are not included as rows because they do not directly measure the tested versions' image power-law exponents or setup dependence in a reported numerical form.

untested.parts: All: no language-model loss, and no parameter, token or compute sweep.
All: no extrapolation of fits from small runs to larger ones.
All: widths are varied, but not at fixed parameter count, and no loss-versus-shape law is fitted.
Whether the power-law form actually holds for image classification: the form is assumed, and no fit quality or deviation is reported.
Dependence of published language-model exponents or splits on parameter counting, schedule, data or fitting method.

record.verdict_notes: The record treated the fitted exponents as evidence for V5 and V7. But the study assumes the power-law form and uses β only to rank models, and its target is the NTK approximation. It also measures image error, not language-model loss. Many comparator rows (R6, R9, R13, R14, R17, R18) repeat the same kernel value. The text's Figure 4 references conflict between 4(b) and 4(c), and between K32k and K64k. Rows R2, R3, R6, R9, R13–R15, R17–R20, R22 and R23 are kernel comparators rather than trained networks.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out pretraining loss and scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small language-model runs predict substantially larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations, and their growth with compute.
Architecture comparisons at a fixed parameter count.

The study tests sample-size scaling of image-classification test error, not cross-entropy loss; it does not test language models, other modalities beyond images, or repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer regimes.
Downstream-task performance as a function of language-model scale or pretraining loss.
Language-model-specific fit choices, parameter counting, data and training schedules, disagreements between the original language-model studies, and compute-optimal allocation.

rows.locator: Section 3; Figure 1(A); Appendix A.2 and A.4
rows.note: The text reports this exponent for the neural network; neural-network results were averaged over 4 random initializations.
rows.check: The exponent .307 is an assumed-form fit to image test error, used to compare against NTKs. No fit quality is reported, so it cannot show whether a power law holds (V5). The variation it shows is across training hyperparameters of the same model, not across the published-law fitting choices V7 names.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Image-classification data scaling on CIFAR-5m-bin and SVHN-parity
reader_labels.reason: The study fits and reports data-scaling constants for finite neural networks on both image tasks (R1, R4, R5, R7, R8, R10, R11, R12, R16, R21). This supports a limited image-classification sample-scaling instance, not the language-model loss or compute-scaling claim.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Reported neural-network scaling constants vary across learning-rate and optimization choices, including .307, .333, .262, .294, .310, .292, and .204 (R1, R7, R8, R10, R11, R12, R16). The paper also describes the results as retaining the neural-network advantage under several practical changes.
